cards.explanation: The answer is that the mountain is raised above the hills, friends. Isaiah says the mountain of the house of the LORD "…will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills…" The hills get a front-row seat to look up at it. That's the picture for the last days.

The answer is False, friends. Isaiah says "…all nations will stream to it." Then he says many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD…" (Isa 2:3). That's a much bigger crowd than one nation.

The answer is that He will teach them His ways, friends. The peoples say, "He will teach us His ways so that we may walk in His paths." Teaching is what they say He will do for them. That's the answer on the board.

The answer is True, friends. The verse says, "For the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem." Zion and Jerusalem both get named right there as where the law and the word go out from. No mystery about the address.

The answer is that they beat them into plowshares, friends. Isaiah says, "They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks." Swords become plowshares and spears become pruning hooks. Same metal, new job.

The answer is war, friends. Isaiah says, "Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war." Nation against nation, and no training for war either. That's a quiet day at the practice field.

The answer is to walk in the light of the LORD, friends. The prophet says, "Come, O house of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD." It comes right after the picture of the nations streaming to the mountain. Jacob's house gets invited to walk in that light.

The answer is that they're filled with influences from the east, friends. The prophet says the LORD has abandoned His people "…because they are filled with influences from the east…" It's right there in verse 6. Filled up to the brim.
The answer is True, friends. Verse 7 says, "Their land is full of silver and gold, with no limit to their treasures…" Full is the word. The prophet isn't being shy about it.
The answer is idols, friends. The prophet says, "Their land is full of idols…" Full of silver, full of horses, and full of idols too. The land is packed.
The answer is False, friends. This is a heavy verse. It says mankind is brought low and man is humbled. Then it says, "…do not forgive them!" There's no request for forgiveness there.

The answer is in the rocks and the dust, friends. Verse 10 says, "Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty." The hiding spot is rocks and dust. That's not a cozy place.

The blanks are humbled and exalted, friends. Verse 11 says, "The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men brought low…" Then it says, "the LORD alone will be exalted in that day." Alone, friends, so nobody else is sharing that spot.

The answer is all the proud and lofty, friends. Verse 12 says, "For the Day of the LORD of Hosts will come against all the proud and lofty, against all that is exalted…" Everything that's lifted up gets humbled. It's a day aimed at pride.
The answer is vanish, friends. Verse 18 says, "…and the idols will vanish completely." Gone. Not one left behind.

The answer is False, friends. Verse 19 says men flee "…away from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth." The verse doesn't mention an army at all.

The answer is the moles and the bats, friends. Verse 20 says men "…cast away to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold…" Silver and gold idols, tossed to the moles and bats. That's quite a turn for something people once bowed down to.

The answer is that man only has breath in his nostrils, friends. Verse 22 says, "Put no more trust in man, who has only the breath in his nostrils." Then it asks, "Of what account is he?" The prophet is saying man isn't the one to lean on.
